question: Explain why no steady electric current flows in a conductor unless an electric field is maintained inside it.

options.A: Without an electric field, free electrons have only random motion with zero average velocity, so there is no net charge flow; a maintained electric field produces drift velocity and hence steady current.
options.B: A steady current flows without an electric field because random electron motion always has a fixed direction.
options.C: An electric field stops electron motion, which allows a steady current to flow.
options.D: A steady current requires no charge carriers; it is produced only by lattice vibrations.
